name: DataBank Dallas Empire Central Data Center

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: This facility is attributed to DataBank, whose own company site confirms active operations across a wide United States footprint including the West (Irvine, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Salt Lake City, San Diego, Seattle, Silicon Valley), Central (Chicago, Denver, Indianapolis, Kansas City, Minneapolis), South (Atlanta, Austin, Dallas, Houston, Memphis, Miami, Waco), and East (Boston, Cleveland, New Jersey, New York City, Northern Virginia, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh) regions, plus the United Kingdom. Every state where this registry lists a DataBank facility, Utah, Virginia, Texas, California, and Nevada, matches a market named on the company own site. The company page also references a partnership with Goodman Group to open a Los Angeles data center. No founding date, headquarters address, ownership structure, or acquisition history, and no building specific address or individual MW figures for this particular registry row, were located in available sourcing this session.
profile.research_note: Market presence confirmed via operator own site, but founding, ownership (e.g. possible DigitalBridge connection), and acquisition history not confirmed this session. Revisit with fresh WebSearch budget.

reading.body:
DataBank Dallas Empire Central sits at 1100 Empire Central Place in Dallas with 4 MW of published IT capacity across 35,900 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 4 MW of IT load supports roughly 100 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, that same load supports roughly 400 racks. The gap between those two figures matters: which end of that range applies here is not published. Four megawatts is a modest footprint by current AI infrastructure standards, where single training clusters routinely consume multiples of that figure.

The campus holds a FedRAMP certification, which qualifies it to host federal cloud workloads under the U.S. government's security authorization framework. No other certifications are published on the operator's spec page.

Texas has 133 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which only 13 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 389 MW across those 13 sites. Empire Central ranks thirteenth out of those thirteen by published IT capacity, meaning it is the smallest campus in the state for which this site holds a published number. Its 4 MW represents roughly one percent of the 389 MW published across Texas facilities tracked here. For a reader evaluating AI scale, this campus is not a major compute concentration; its FedRAMP qualification makes it relevant to regulated federal workloads rather than to large-scale AI training or inference deployment.
